conventions.frame: Mars, IAU 2000; USGS Gazetteer MDIM 2.1 control network
Mars 2000 sphere (R = 3,396,190 m), equirectangular; Mars Trek
conventions.note: On a sphere, planetocentric and planetographic latitude coincide, so the sphere CRS fixes the convention.

conventions.frame: Mars; PDS Mars 2020 sample dossier, Initial Reports vol. 4
conventions.note: The source states only "Latitude (N), Longitude (E), Elevation". It does not state the latitude type, datum or elevation reference. Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude on the Mars 2000 frame, with elevation relative to the areoid, is INFERRED from the cross-checks below. It is not confirmed by complete authoritative CRS metadata.

conventions.frame: Mars 2000 geographic (ArcGIS wkid 104905, GCS_Mars_2000); Mars Trek traverse service
conventions.note: The service states the Mars 2000 geographic CRS, but not whether latitude is planetocentric or planetographic. Its GeoJSON output is mislabelled "EPSG:4326"; the values are Mars degrees and must not be reprojected with Earth parameters. Planetocentric latitude is INFERRED from the cross-checks below.

crossValidation.reproduce: Unit tests in src/lib/geo/geo-data.test.ts (sample sites vs traverse) and `npm run verify:geo` (live: traverse attributes and CTX DTM elevations at the sample sites).
crossValidation.reasoning: The PDS sample coordinates, the Trek traverse and the Trek sphere-based CTX DTM come from separate products. Mixing planetocentric and planetographic latitude at 18.5° N would shift positions by about 12 km. Agreement at metre level therefore supports a shared planetocentric convention.

checks.description: Distance from each PDS sample site to the nearest point on the Trek traverse
checks.result: 2.2–2.5 m for all three sites (raw traverse vertices, 2026-11-05)
checks.threshold: ≤ 5 m (unit test, against the committed simplified traverse)

checks.description: PDS sample elevation minus CTX DTM elevation (20 m grid, areoid-referenced, Mars 2000 sphere) at the sample position
checks.result: Pelican Point +1.8 m, Lefroy Bay +3.6 m, Comet Geyser +3.0 m (npm run verify:geo, 2026-11-05)
checks.threshold: ≤ 10 m (verify:geo; the 20 m DTM cannot resolve metre-scale relief)
